research_question: Do statement-structure features improve genuinely prospective Codeforces rating prediction beyond contest-index position alone?

include: Codeforces contests whose scheduled start is inside the fixed eligibility window
every problem index explicitly captured from the public contest interface at T0
problems later classified as PROGRAMMING that receive an official numeric rating
exclude: unrated contests or problems without an official numeric rating by cohort close
cohort.close_rule: Close at the eligibility end timestamp, but do not run the confirmatory analysis unless both minimum sample thresholds are met; otherwise report the cohort as underpowered without extending it post hoc.
cohort.operational_misses: A contest with incomplete T0 capture or prediction is retained in the operational coverage denominator and recorded as missed; it is never silently dropped or partially predicted.
cohort.cohort_census_rule: Starting at the frozen census anchor, request the official Codeforces contest.list endpoint with gym=false and lang=en. Seal the first response that passes only the frozen transport and basic-structure predicate. Every in-window contest must map exactly once to a locked prediction set or an operational miss; there is no discretionary contest-exclusion category. Any unmapped, multiply mapped, or ledger-extra contest is a cohort-integrity failure and blocks confirmatory analysis.

prediction_timepoint.name: T0
prediction_timepoint.definition: After the public problem statement is available and before this project reads or joins the official problem rating.
prediction_timepoint.clock_policy: Capture and prediction CLIs obtain UTC from the system clock and expose no timestamp override. They check before and after exclusive publication; an operation crossing the deadline retains no model input or prediction.
prediction_timepoint.public_commitment: The sanitized input hash, capture-sidecar hash, prediction hash, and append-only ledger event must reach the repository default branch before the T0 lock deadline. Record a GitHub Actions push-event run id, URL, and GitHub-created timestamp at or before the deadline as the external time witness; local Git author or committer dates are insufficient. A late or missing witness makes the whole contest an operational miss.
prediction_timepoint.coverage_event_witness: A direct operational miss is also a base coverage event with the same lock deadline and must receive the same GitHub push-run witness. A missing or late miss witness remains publicly visible as untimely coverage rather than being silently backdated.

external_timestamp.witness_record_policy: Preserve the exact GitHub workflow-run API response and append a normalized witness event in a later commit. The GitHub-created timestamp of the first successful attempt for the immutable target commit is the deadline evidence; the workflow may finish and the normalized witness may be appended after the deadline.

model_bundle.training_population: All eligible historical rows strictly before cohort.eligibility_start_utc; historical train, validation, and test labels are treated only as development data for this new future cohort.
model_bundle.numeric_preprocessing: Per-feature median imputation, then population-variance standardization; constants use scale 1.
model_bundle.freeze_requirement: After this draft is reviewed, freeze and test the confirmatory analysis implementation, then change status to frozen, record the freeze timestamp, and commit the protocol, analysis code, JSON model bundle, runtime manifest, hashes, and source commit before the first eligible prediction.

outcome.reveal_source: Codeforces problemset.problems queried only by the separate reveal step
outcome.rating_version_rule: Per-contest reveal may append the first rating snapshot obtained no earlier than 72 hours for audit. For the confirmatory outcome, begin five minutes after eligibility_end_utc plus 72 hours and use the first successful full problemset.problems snapshot, retrying every 30 minutes for at most 24 hours; commit its SHA-256 before analysis. A rating absent from that snapshot is missing for the primary analysis. If no snapshot succeeds by the deadline, do not choose a later version or run confirmatory analysis. Later official revisions are descriptive amendments only.
outcome.rounding: Predictions remain floating point in the ledger; no rounding before metric calculation.

cohort_census.first_success_predicate: HTTP success, parseable JSON, top-level status OK, list result, and unique integer contest ids with integer startTimeSeconds; cohort membership and prediction coverage are evaluated only after selection.

confirmatory_outcome.first_success_predicate: HTTP success, parseable JSON, top-level status OK, object result with a problems list, and a unique positive-integer contestId plus non-empty index on every problem record; ratings, prediction matches, sample size, and cohort integrity are evaluated only after selection.

confirmatory_analysis.primary_estimand: Mean paired absolute-error improvement: index-only comparator absolute error minus text-light model absolute error.
confirmatory_analysis.uncertainty: Two-sided 95% percentile interval from the frozen contest-cluster bootstrap.
confirmatory_analysis.paired_improvement_definition: abs(official_rating - comparator_prediction) - abs(official_rating - primary_prediction); positive values favor the primary model.

bootstrap.contest_order: normalized positive-integer contest_id values sorted by integer value ascending
bootstrap.draw_operation: Call rng.integers(0, contest_count, size=(10000, contest_count), endpoint=False, dtype=np.int64) exactly once before any other random-number use.
bootstrap.replicate_statistic: Expanded problem-level mean: include every paired row in each sampled contest once per cluster draw, preserving cluster multiplicity.

confirmatory_analysis.analysis_input_validation: Require unique contest_id,index prediction keys, one matching outcome at most, finite predictions, and no duplicate contest clusters. Exclude missing official ratings without imputation and report their count. Fail rather than silently repair malformed or duplicate rows.
confirmatory_analysis.minimum_threshold_population: The minimum 30 contests and 200 problems are counted only among distinct contests and paired problem rows that have both locked primary/comparator predictions and a rating in the single cohort-close outcome snapshot. Operational misses remain in the coverage denominator but do not count toward thresholds or bootstrap samples.
confirmatory_analysis.analysis_execution_gate: The deterministic confirmatory-analysis implementation and fixture tests must be committed before protocol freeze. Refuse all aggregate metrics and bootstrap work before earliest_execution_utc, unless the frozen census/outcome selections and mapping integrity all verify, or when fewer than 30 distinct paired contests or 200 paired rows remain.

secondary_metrics.problem_level_mae: Arithmetic mean absolute error over all paired problem rows, reported separately for primary and comparator predictions.
secondary_metrics.contest_macro_mae: Compute model MAE within each contest, then take the unweighted arithmetic mean across distinct contests.
secondary_metrics.within_100_accuracy: Fraction of paired rows with absolute error less than or equal to 100.
secondary_metrics.within_200_accuracy: Fraction of paired rows with absolute error less than or equal to 200.

index_rank_bands.A-B: normalized alphabetic index prefix A or B
index_rank_bands.C-D: normalized alphabetic index prefix C or D
index_rank_bands.E+: normalized alphabetic index prefix E or later

golden_fixture.cluster_values: For integer i from 0 through 29, cluster i contains the single value i + i*i/1000.

confirmatory_analysis.multiplicity: Only the paired MAE improvement is confirmatory; all secondary and subgroup results are descriptive.
confirmatory_analysis.missing_outcomes: Do not impute ratings. Report eligible predictions lacking a rating separately and exclude them from metric denominators.
confirmatory_analysis.no_peeking_rule: Do not calculate aggregate prospective performance or alter model, features, exclusions, endpoints, or thresholds before cohort close.

amendments: While status is draft, changes remain reviewable in Git history. From the commit that changes status to frozen, never edit this file in place. Any later change, even before the first prediction, requires a new protocol_id and future cohort; document deviations without deleting prior evidence.

supersedes.reason: The v1 workflow lacked a dedicated label-isolated T0 capture command and schema-before-values validation.

input_capture.source: Public Codeforces problem statement pages constructed only from an explicit contest_id and explicit problem indices.
input_capture.decode_policy: Decode raw statement bytes as UTF-8 with replacement for invalid byte sequences; response Content-Type and final redirect URL are audit-only fields.
input_capture.metadata_api_policy: Do not call Codeforces problemset metadata APIs, read a local metadata table, or join labels, points, tags, solved counts, submissions, acceptances, or verdicts at T0.
input_capture.index_entry_policy: The operator must enter every problem index visible in the public contest interface; contest_start_utc and the index list are recorded as explicit operator inputs and verified only after reveal.
input_capture.post_reveal_verification: The reveal step must verify the scheduled start and complete problem-index list against the official contest record. Any mismatch makes the whole contest an operational miss; never add or correct prediction rows post hoc.
input_capture.model_input_schema: Exactly contest_id,index followed by the 41 protocol statement feature columns in frozen order. Derived index features are computed by the predictor. Fetch status, URLs, timestamps, hashes, and errors belong only in the capture sidecar.
input_capture.completeness_rule: All requested statements must be freshly fetched and parsed. Any failure invalidates the whole contest input and is recorded as an operational miss; partial prediction is prohibited.
input_capture.immutability_rule: Capture input, raw pages, sidecar, model artifacts, and prediction outputs use no-overwrite publication semantics.
